title: Map with Legend: Annotated Maps That Explain
description: Build a Map with Legend — labelled markers and coloured regions, each added with a click and listed in an auto-generated legend with swatches. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a flood-action group marks three sandbag stores, two rest centres and the streets that flood first — and the legend writes itself as they click.
quick_answer: The Map with Legend builder lets you add labelled markers and coloured regions to a map, one click each, while a legend builds itself beside the map — every entry with its colour swatch. Share the finished annotated map by link when it is ready to explain itself.
steps_intro: Every thing you add appears twice: on the map, and in the legend that explains it:

body.t: Flood plans, festival layouts, consultation proposals — maps a mixed audience must read without a briefing. The legend is the briefing, built in.
Regions coloured by type, sites numbered in the legend — students arrive knowing the code. Print the result via
Territories as regions, outlets as markers, one legend to bind them — the honest version of the wall map with pins, made shareable. Bulk CSV points belong in
Stages, gates, first aid, parking — coloured regions for zones and pins for points, legible to every volunteer who opens the link.

Blue regions for the streets that flood first, house icons for sandbag stores, a hall for the rest centre. A resident opens the link and understands their street's plan in under a minute — the legend did that.
Current catchment in green, proposed in amber, the school as a star. Parents argue about the proposal looking at the same picture — which is what consultation maps are for.

popular_table.title: Legend craft in four rules
popular_table.intro: An auto-generated legend is only as clear as the entries you feed it.
rows: The legend is read first by strangers
Colour by category, not by whim
Same colour must mean same thing
Regions for areas, pins for points
Flood extent shaded; pump sites pinned
Past ~12 entries, group or split the map
Two maps beat one crowded legend
popular_table.note: The annotated map shares via a link that encodes your entries — no account and no server copy. Whoever holds the link sees the map, so share it the way you would share the document itself.

faq: Can I remove or rename an entry?
Yes — entries stay editable while you build: rename the label, change the colour, or delete the item from map and legend together. The shared link reflects the state when you copy it.
They can — overlapping areas are sometimes the story (a proposed zone inside a current one). Semi-transparent fills keep both visible; the legend lists each on its own row.
Export the composed view as a PNG for handouts. For classroom printing at a designed scale, the Printable Map with Scale Context tool frames paper output properly.
Can I import entries from a spreadsheet?
This builder is for hand-built, story-first maps. Data-first work starts in CSV to Map; bring the handful of entries that need storytelling here afterwards.
The link encodes the map's state rather than pointing at a stored file, so it works while the tool's link format is supported. For the permanent record, export a PNG as well.
Can I use my organisation's colours?
Pick the closest swatches the builder offers; exact brand matching is presentation-software work — export the PNG and finish the design there if the brand police are strict.
A standard open street map under your annotations (OpenStreetMap data). Your layer carries the meaning; the base stays neutral and current.
